title: Full-minus-subset drought richness slopes were uncertain in four US desert bird samples in 1998-2022
abstract: We tested whether annual drought slopes differ between supplied full-survey richness and richness from a released bird count subset. We used 714 route-years in four US desert spatial and time samples from 1998 to 2022. Models controlled route, year, survey date and land cover. All four direct full-minus-subset slope intervals crossed zero after adjustment for 12 tests. Estimates ranged from -0.652 to +0.140 species per unit lower annual SPEI. Identity-group, roster-size and year-effect checks did not resolve the difference. All full and subset slope intervals also crossed zero. This new paired contrast uses the same release as a prior campaign rarefaction study. It is not an independent data replication. Selected records, detection, few year clusters and large uncertainty prevent a causal or equivalence claim. Code, aggregate evidence, source hashes, retrieval instructions and independent variance checks are included. Pollution was not tested.
